new23: Observed and predicted weight at age, 2014–2028, after omitting 2026 BTS weight observations from the standalone random-effects fit. Cell labels give mean weight in kg per fish for ages 3–10. Fishery and BTS observations end in 2025; the right-hand panel includes 2026 estimates without weight observations and 2027–2028 forecasts. The solid line marks 2026; dashed boxes mark forecast years. Colours show proportional deviations from each age’s mean through 2025 within its own panel, saturating at ±50%. Blank cells indicate absent observations, including the 2020 BTS gap. This figure describes the selected fit; it provides no direct comparison with the fit that included 2026 BTS weights.
new34: Model 26.0 biological and selectivity schedules. Maturity, female fraction and natural mortality are supplied inputs. The weight panel distinguishes the 2026 population (BTS), spawning and fishery schedules from the selected 2027 fishery forecast used for both catch and spawning in projections. The 2026 fishery estimates and 2027 forecast come from the standalone WtAgeRE fit omitting 2026 BTS weight observations; population and historical spawning weights retain their separate treatments. Fishing and survey selectivity curves have approximate 95% asymptotic ranges; ATS and AVO share their estimated curve. Supplied schedules have no fitted-parameter bands.
alt23: Three heatmaps for 2014–2028 compare observed fishery weights, observed BTS weights, and predicted fishery-scale weights. Observations end in 2025. The 2026 age-3 cohort has predicted weights of 0.37 kg in 2026, 0.48 kg at age 4 in 2027, and 0.60 kg at age 5 in 2028. Boundaries identify 2026 and forecast years.
